20: [PGlite filesystem documentation](https://github.com/electric-sql/pglite/blob/main/docs/docs/filesystems.md) says IndexedDB loads database files into memory and flushes changed files after queries; relaxed durability schedules flushing asynchronously. Its [worker example](https://github.com/electric-sql/pglite/blob/main/packages/pglite/examples/worker.html) exposes leader changes. This supports a deliberate single-owner lifecycle but does not certify shared-workstation PHI persistence or PatientGPT multi-window recovery. [SurrealDB embedded Rust documentation](https://github.com/surrealdb/docs.surrealdb.com/blob/main/src/content/build/embedding/by-language/rust.mdx) distinguishes memory from persistent file engines; engine availability alone does not supply clinical authority, tenancy, or synchronization semantics.

22: ## Identity and edge integration
23: 
24: Kratos supplies identity/session validation. Flint Gate supplies request authentication, authorization, claims enrichment, and stream enforcement, analogous to the identity access proxy role of Oathkeeper. Envoy Gateway supplies ingress routing and can delegate authorization to a separate service. These are distinct ownership seams.
25: 
26: - `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/flint-gate/crates/flint-gate-core/src/auth/kratos.rs:97-147,194-200` accepts one Authorization or configured session-cookie credential and rejects competing credentials. It does not select `x-session-token` in that function.
27: - `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/TribeHealth/kevin/prior-auth/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/session.rs:69-121` forwards cookies or native `x-session-token` to whoami, handles 401/403/unavailability distinctly, and creates a user principal. Delegated agents need a separate provider. This is an actual adapter mismatch to settle at the shared auth contract, not a reason to equate a clinician with an agent.
28: - `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/TribeHealth/kevin/prior-auth/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/kratos_proxy.rs:28-35,55-88` proxies browser login/recovery and preserves cookie/redirect headers. A deployed native login/logout and secure credential lifecycle was not exercised here.
29: - Official [Kratos sessions](https://github.com/ory/docs/blob/master/docs/kratos/session-management/01_overview.mdx) documents cookie/native session validation. Official [Oathkeeper integration](https://github.com/ory/docs/blob/master/docs/kratos/guides/zero-trust-iap-proxy-identity-access-proxy.mdx) uses the cookie-session authenticator against whoami. These do not make every native header accepted by every local adapter.
30: - Official [Envoy Gateway external authorization](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/tasks/security/ext-auth) configures `SecurityPolicy.extAuth.http` and allowed identity headers to the backend. [API reference](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/api/extension_types) says HTTP authorization forwards a limited default header set; cookie forwarding therefore needs deliberate configuration. Fail-open behavior and actual installed CRD semantics must be checked before implementation.
31: - The inspected Flint Gate checkout (`39c40d6`) identifies itself as an Oathkeeper replacement in `README.md:7`, but searching its Rust source for `ext_authz`, `ext-authz`, and Envoy produced no implementation match. Do not assert this checkout exposes a working Envoy check endpoint. It may differ from the deployed digest or another branch.

Flint Gate and Forge each had two ready replicas, Fabric one, Kratos one at `oryd/kratos:v26.2.0`.
